title: Analytical STEM Study of Bi2O3 Catalyst for Selective Chemical Looping Combustion
content: The ability to selectively oxidize one hydrocarbon in a mixture of hydrocarbons using a catalyst can provide immense flexibility in purifying gas streams relevant for making fuels and chemicals [1,2]. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of surface reactions mandates concurrently a comprehensive understanding of the primary catalytic material used in the reaction [3,4]. In this study, we discuss the evolution of the atomic structure and morphology of a bismuth oxide (Bi2O3) catalyst through the various phases of the selective oxidation reaction of acetylene in ethylene-rich streams [5].
